note: 204/5-01's FIRST FLIGHT, AND IT IS A PARTIAL ROW -- filed before analysis, per this folder's standing rule. What it MEASURES: the panel path on a real phone, with the context actually running (`audio.availability` = running, checked first), 97.5 s of a 150-unit / 40-call board. What it CANNOT measure, and the reason is an instrument defect rather than a device limit: NO CAR IS VOICED. `audio.vehicles` is 0 and `units.unvoiced` is 150, because this pak (built 28-08-2026) carries none of `data/gtasa_vehicleAudioSettings.cfg`, `data/vehicles.ide`, `data/handling.cfg` -- and `loadAudio` turns each missing file into an empty map with NOTHING reported. So the world bus was empty all run, the pool never rose above 2 live voices out of 64, and the row's headline number (`refusedByBus.cad` = 0 UNDER LOAD) is true here and says nothing: the reserve was never asked for. The same goes for `peakSample`: 0.7688 is -2.29 dBFS, but of a single panel tone near its own full scale, NOT of the 64 summed voices 204/1-02's -4.8 dBFS arithmetic is about. Neither confirms nor refutes that prediction. `maxLatencyMs` is 0 BY CONSTRUCTION and not by speed: `map` events are raised locally with no arrival timestamp, and the CAD stand-in does not pass one either, so the 50 ms budget has no instrument yet. What IS readable and real: the audio clock's cost, the panel's own counts, the coalescing ratio, and the frame beside them.

readable.audioClockVerdict: mean 0.70 ms passes the 2 ms budget with room; max 7.5 ms blows it 3.7x. One tick in ~976 costing 7.5 ms is 0.75% of a second, so it is not a frame problem -- but the budget is stated per TICK and this run does not meet it. Which tick costs it is not in the report and would have to be found.
readable.coalescingRatio: 96 folded against 32 played -- 3 of every 4 raised events were a repeat inside the 900 ms per-name window. On a 150-unit board that is the feature working, not a fault.

the output peak of a full mix -- 1/02's -4.8 dBFS prediction is untouched
event -> audible ms against 50 -- no event in this build carries an arrival timestamp
MB against 64 -- buffers.bytes is 0, because no car sound was ever fetched
the battery delta against boardsilent -- one half only; power.charging was TRUE all run, so a delta taken from it would have been worthless anyway
203/4-03's engine and siren numbers -- same cause
verdict: The flight was worth taking and the row is not the row. It found a SILENT absence instead: three data files the vehicle voice table needs are missing from this pak and nothing says so, which made a 150-unit board sound like an empty one while every field in the report stayed plausible. That is the exact failure shape this folder's rules are written about -- a complete, self-consistent capture of the wrong thing. Fix the instrument (report the missing files; carry an arrival timestamp), get a pak that carries the data, then re-fly the pair in one thermal window on battery.
